test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 18 Aug 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

1. Some avalanches are precipitations.

2. Some cataclysms are avalanches.

3. All avalanches are storms.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some storms are cataclysms.

II. No precipitation is storms.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

solution:
Given Statements:

1. Some avalanches are precipitations.

2. Some cataclysms are avalanches.

3. All avalanches are storms.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c2cef61d646f060074de5b9b383e91630128fea16f9ff2942ff2d0f8accd650d.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some storms are cataclysms → True (Because it is given that some cataclysms are avalanches and all avalanches are storms which means there is definitely some part of storms that is cataclysms.)

II. No precipitation is storms → False (Because it is given that some avalanches are precipitations and all avalanches are storms which means definitely some precipitation are storm.)

So, only conclusion I follows.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**.
